title: Betulinic Acid Reduces Intestinal Inflammation and Enhances Intestinal Tight Junctions by Modulating the PPAR-gamma/NF-kappaB Signaling Pathway in Intestinal Cells and Organoids.
authors: Zheng, Xu; Cao, Zhen; Wang, Mingqi; Yuan, Ruqiang; Han, Yinhe; Li, Ang; Wang, Xiuli
one_liner_zh: 该文研究桦木酸通过PPAR-γ/NF-κB通路改善肠道炎症和紧密连接，仅含分子对接初步预测，非蛋白质-DNA互作核心，且无AI或物理模拟方法。
abstract: Background: Intestinal epithelial barrier (IEB) dysfunction is related to multiple gastrointestinal disorders, notably inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Betulinic acid (BA), a compound derived from birch bark, has demonstrated potential therapeutic benefits in IBD. Nevertheless, the impact of BA on IEB function has not been fully elucidated. Methods: The current study aimed to explore the potential underlying mechanisms of BA in dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced IBD in mice and co-culture models involving Caco-2/HT29-MTX-E12 cell monolayers or mouse intestinal organoids (IOs) in conjunction with macrophages stimulated by lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Results: In vivo, BA treatment significantly improved body weight and colon length, alleviated disease activity index (DAI) scores, and reduced colonic histopathological injury in IBD mice. In vitro, BA reduced the flux of FITC-dextran; increased the TEER; and decreased the production of IL-6, IL-1beta, and TNF-alpha while increasing IL-10 mRNA levels. Additionally, BA enhanced IEB formation by upregulating ZO-1, occludin (OCLN), and claudin-1 (CLDN1). Molecular docking studies revealed significant docking scores and interactions between BA and PPAR-gamma. Moreover, BA significantly upregulated PPAR-gamma protein expression, decreased NF-kappaB and MLC2 phosphorylation, and reduced MLCK protein expression. However, this effect was reversed by GW9662, an effective PPAR-gamma antagonist. Conclusions: The findings reveal that BA mitigates IBD by safeguarding the intestinal barrier against dysfunction. This effect may be attributed to its ability to suppress inflammation and enhance the expression of tight junction proteins by modulating the PPAR-gamma/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: 背景：肠上皮屏障（IEB）功能障碍与多种胃肠道疾病相关，尤其是炎症性肠病（IBD）。桦木酸（BA）是一种源自桦树皮的化合物，在IBD中显示出潜在的治疗益处。然而，BA对IEB功能的影响尚未完全阐明。方法：本研究旨在探讨BA在葡聚糖硫酸钠（DSS）诱导的IBD小鼠模型及涉及Caco-2/HT29-MTX-E12细胞单层或小鼠肠道类器官（IOs）与脂多糖（LPS）刺激的巨噬细胞共培养模型中的潜在作用机制。结果：在体内实验中，BA治疗显著改善了IBD小鼠的体重和结肠长度，减轻了疾病活动指数（DAI）评分，并减少了结肠组织病理学损伤。在体外实验中，BA降低了FITC-葡聚糖的通量；增加了TEER；降低了IL-6、IL-1β和TNF-α的产生，同时增加了IL-10 mRNA水平。此外，BA通过上调ZO-1、occludin（OCLN）和claudin-1（CLDN1）增强了IEB的形成。分子对接研究揭示了BA与PPAR-γ之间显著的对接评分和相互作用。此外，BA显著上调了PPAR-γ蛋白表达，降低了NF-κB和MLC2的磷酸化，并减少了MLCK蛋白表达。然而，这种效应被有效的PPAR-γ拮抗剂GW9662所逆转。结论：研究结果表明，BA通过保护肠道屏障免受功能障碍来缓解IBD。这一效应可能归因于其通过调节PPAR-γ/NF-κB信号通路来抑制炎症并增强紧密连接蛋白表达的能力。
